reason: At the base revision, lone 'Y' and 'YYY' fall through to the timezone-offset fallback (REGEX_FORMAT matches Y{1,4} but format() only implements YY/YYYY), so 'Y' renders as a UTC offset rather than the literal letter.
The PR narrows REGEX_FORMAT to YYYY/YY and preserves other year tokens literally, so a lone 'Y' outputs 'Y' and 'YYY' outputs two-digit-year plus 'Y', matching the expected result.
This is a behavior-preserving refactor (extracting tryDecodeURIComponent), so percent-encoded route parameters still decode to the original character.
Same refactor as base; decoding behavior is unchanged, so the handler still reads the decoded space rather than '%20'.
At base, reschedule writes the new score to Redis via zincrby but never updates @score, so the in-memory handle keeps reporting the stale pre-reschedule time.
The fix sets @score = at.to_f after zincrby, so the same in-memory handle immediately reflects the new reschedule time.
Content-Type charset parsing is unrelated to the Range-header whitespace change, so it still reports text/plain with charset UTF-8 as expected.
The Range-header change does not touch Content-Type parsing, so charset detection behaves identically and the test still passes.
Zip archive timestamp preservation is unrelated to the ComposerRepository logging change, so archiving still preserves source modification times.
Re-archiving behavior is unaffected by the logging-only change, so both extractions retain source-matching timestamps.
JSON deserialization is unrelated to the CredentialCache case-sensitivity change, so async deserialization still completes successfully.
The CredentialCache change does not affect System.Text.Json, so sync and async deserialization still produce equivalent results.
INET <<= ANY is unrelated to the FETCH FIRST cursor fix, so the query still parses and returns true without a syntax error.
The INET >>= ANY query is unaffected by the cursor change and still executes correctly, returning true.
At base, every NO_PROXY entry is wildcard-prefixed as a domain pattern, mangling '::1' into a form the URL parser rejects, so client construction raises.
The fix detects IPv6 hostnames and mounts 'all://[::1]', so client construction with NO_PROXY='::1' succeeds.
At base the GH-63108 follow-up broke all flags except IGNORECASE, so requesting DOTALL raises instead of matching 'a\nc' and not 'ac'.
The fix restores DOTALL and other flags, so 'a.c' with dot-matches-newline matches 'a\nc' and not 'ac', both via flags= and a compiled pattern.
At base, a group mid-chain with more than two following tasks gets wrong recursive result parents, so serialization/reconstruction loses some of the four child results.
The fix updates prev_task/prev_res after each group, so reconstruction preserves all four child results across the two parallel groups.
The PR only fixes the '-- as first argument' case; the trailing '--' handoff after value1 value2 already worked at base, so both positionals populate correctly and this is unaffected.
The added value-terminator branch does not break the trailing handoff, so the first positional still gets value1/value2 and the second gets --check.
At base, nvim_set_option_value('background') runs without :noautocmd, so a post-startup OSC 11 response fires OptionSet (and ColorScheme) as the test expects.
The fix wraps the background set in :noautocmd to suppress OptionSet, so the test's expectation that OptionSet/ColorScheme fire no longer holds.
Changeset required-field validation is unrelated to the @derive compile-time reordering, so an omitted required field still yields an invalid changeset with a 'can't be blank' error.
The @derive reordering does not change validation logic, so the changeset is still flagged invalid for the blank required field.
